note: Domestic service credentials (FR-SEC-02). Foreign scanners key on GitHub, AWS, and Slack shapes and miss these entirely, which is the point of the file. Add a service by appending one entry here; no TypeScript change is needed. 'signature' entries match the credential's own distinctive shape, 'context' entries need a nearby keyword because the raw value is indistinguishable from an ordinary identifier. Every sample in attack-lab/datasets/korean-service-tokens.json is synthetic.

credentials.basis: Toss Payments issues server-side keys with a fixed test_sk_ or live_sk_ prefix, so the prefix alone identifies the credential without any surrounding keyword.

Same prefix scheme as the secret key. A client key is meant to reach the browser, so it is scored lower than a secret key — but it still identifies a merchant and should not travel through an Agent transcript unmasked.
Kakao's REST APIs authenticate with an 'Authorization: KakaoAK <key>' header. The KakaoAK scheme name is unique to Kakao, so the header form is unambiguous.

A Kakao app key is 32 lowercase hex characters, which is also what an MD5 digest looks like. Matching the bare value would flag every checksum in a log, so this entry requires the assignment keyword and the signature entry above covers the header form. The field name may be quoted, as it is in a JSON body.

credentials.service: 네이버 클라우드 플랫폼 / NAVER Cloud Platform
credentials.credential: 서브 계정 액세스 키 / IAM access key
credentials.basis: NAVER Cloud Platform sub-account keys carry an ncp_iam_ prefix that no other vendor uses.
NAVER Open API client secrets are short alphanumeric strings with no distinguishing shape, but they travel in a header whose name is unique to NAVER.

credentials.service: 국내 증권사 Open API / Korean brokerage Open API
credentials.basis: Korean brokerage Open APIs (한국투자증권 등) authenticate with an appkey/appsecret pair whose values carry no vendor prefix. Only the long secret is matched, and only next to its field name: 'appkey' alone is too common a field name to key on safely. This is the weakest entry in the file and the most likely to need a contributor's correction.
